title: Ensure process cleanup on stop update and restart
description: Verify and fix cleanup of child processes, systemd units, listeners, timers, and temporary files across stop, update, restart, and failed deploy.
acceptanceCriteria: Stopping a tunnel removes or disables its owned processes/units and closes local listeners
An update or redeploy disposes the old runtime before activating the replacement without orphan processes
A failed deploy cleans partial files/listeners while retaining the previous active runtime
Cleanup is bounded and reports a nonzero/error event when a resource cannot be disposed

steps.description: Create fixtures for child-process exit, systemd stop failure, listener cleanup, partial deploy, and dispose-during-shutdown.
Map every process handle, listener, timer, and temp file to its owner and disposal path in engine/forwarder/process modules.
Make disposal idempotent and aggregate cleanup errors without leaking secret-bearing command arguments.
Run focused tests and a process/listener inspection fixture; run the full custom harness.

technicalNotes: Do not use broad `pkill` or process-name matching; cleanup must be scoped to the managed handle/unit/listener.
